title: Prefix-match halt result
statement: Let $C,e\in\mathbb{N}$, let $m$ be a Boolean value, let $f$ map finite bit strings to finite bit strings, let $x,b$ be finite bit strings, let $p,B\in\mathbb{N}$, and let $v$ be a vector of fourteen natural-number registers whose values are all at most $B$. On the input encoding $\langle\langle x,b\rangle,\mathrm{bits}(p)\rangle$, the specified machine started in the prefix-hit state with register vector $v$ halts with answer true if $m$ is true, and otherwise with answer equal to the bit of $f(x)$ at index $\lfloor v(0)/2\rfloor$, taking an out-of-range index to have value false. Every configuration before halting satisfies the machine's admissibility condition and has all register values at most $B$.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ maps finite bit strings to finite bit strings
$v$ assigns natural-number values to fourteen registers
Every register value of $v$ is at most $B$
replaced:
Let $C,e\in\mathbb N$, let $\mathrm{mode}$ be Boolean, let $f$ map finite bit strings to
finite bit strings, and let $x,b$ be bit strings and $p,B$ natural numbers. If $v$ is a
vector of fourteen natural-number registers whose entries are all at most $B$, then, on
input $\langle\langle x,b\rangle,\mathrm{bits}(p)\rangle$, the specified machine started
at its prefix-match state with register vector $v$ halts with answer true when
$\mathrm{mode}$ is true, and otherwise returns the bit of $f(x)$ at index $\lfloor
v(0)/2\rfloor$, taking an out-of-range bit to be false. Every configuration before
halting satisfies the machine's precondition and register bound.
